transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-25
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 58 min
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood Partnerships), Priya (Redwood Solutions); Jorge (ZenithMesh), Lena (ZenithMesh Cloud), Omar (ZenithMesh Channel), Nia (ZenithMesh Security)

Summary: quick intro to partnership model, high-level technical compatibility checks (VPC, peering, hardware types), initial channel/rev-share questions and pilot framing. Action items and next steps captured at end.

---
00:00 Jorge (ZenithMesh): Okay thanks everyone for joining, appreciate the time. We're mostly here to see how Redwood could plug into our marketplace/onramp and what a technical integration looks like.
00:14 Alex (Redwood): Totally — thanks Jorge. Super quick intros from our side: I'm Alex on partnerships, Maya is our infra SE who runs most of the hybrid and VPC integrations, Samir supports GTM alignment.
00:28 Lena (ZenithMesh): Lena, cloud architect. We run multi-region PoPs across NA and EU, and we offer both managed GPU fleets and an integrator marketplace.
00:38 Maya (Redwood): Nice, sounds similar to a few partners we work with. High-level question: are you expecting Redwood to be a backend vendor that you route model-serving traffic to, or more of a control-plane integration where you surface Redwood models directly in your UI?
00:52 Omar (ZenithMesh): Probably both? Ideally initially a backend onramp — like route requests to Redwood Dedicated pools for certain tenants — then later a marketplace listing + billing flow.
01:05 Alex (Redwood): Got it. For the backend onramp we typically need either VPC peering + private routing or a TLS-protected API over public internet with mTLS, depending on customer isolation needs. Which is closer to your architecture?
01:21 Lena (ZenithMesh): Most of our enterprise merchants want private connectivity. We use AWS Transit Gateway for a lot of peering; some customers are in GCP. We prefer not to force them through public egress.
01:33 Maya (Redwood): That checks out — Redwood Private supports VPC peering and can sit in a partner's VPC in a deployed mode. Two quick caveats to be aware of: 1) KV cache/affinity — when you do sticky sessions to an instance for low-latency generation, we need predictable routing so KV cache warmness stays beneficial; 2) GPU topology — choice of A100 vs H100 and quantized model variants changes latency/cost profiles.
01:59 Nia (ZenithMesh): On the security side we'll need SOC2 evidence, SAML/SSO integration patterns, and KMS/HSM usage guidance since many of our customers require customer-managed keys.
02:12 Samir (Redwood): Absolutely — we'll share the SOC2 and infra security brief. For KMS we integrate with customer KMS in Private deployments; on hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via partner KMS integrations.
02:25 Jorge (ZenithMesh): A quick commercial question: what's your usual revenue split or pricing model when integrating via a channel partner like us?
02:33 Alex (Redwood): We have a couple of patterns — 1) reseller model where partner bills and we wholesale; 2) marketplace listing where partner takes a % of list price; 3) dedicated reserved capacity where partner helps broker contracts. We can share ranges but final terms often depend on commit size.
02:51 Omar (ZenithMesh): Makes sense. For us the important bit is a clean API contract and a white-labeled-ish experience.
03:02 Priya (Redwood): We have a partner SDK that can sit in your control plane to surface models and usage metrics. It includes per-tenant routing hooks and rate-limiting so you can enforce tenant-level quotas.
03:18 Lena (ZenithMesh): Can you describe the typical network egress patterns and whether you support IP allowlists? We worry about restricting traffic to vendor IPs.
03:28 Maya (Redwood): We do allowlists and peering. For Dedicated we can place the runtime inside your VPC so egress is internal; for hosted we provide a set of egress IP ranges and mTLS certificates. Note that running inside a partner VPC introduces ops considerations for scaling and monitoring.
03:48 Jorge (ZenithMesh): Ops — how much responsibility for autoscaling belongs to us vs Redwood in that co-located model?
03:56 Maya (Redwood): If Redwood manages the runtime in your VPC (managed private), we can run autoscaling but need network access to our control plane for metrics/ops (control plane can be either Redwoods' or a customer-managed control plane depending on contract). If you want the entire control plane on-prem, that's a bigger engineering project.
04:16 Lena (ZenithMesh): Noted. A few technical questions we want looked at in a follow-up deep dive: how does Redwood handle prefix cache invalidation across scale events, and what's the KV cache synchronization model when routing requests across PoPs?
04:28 Maya (Redwood): Good ones. Short answers: prefix and KV caches are per-runtime instance, we do not currently auto-sync KV caches across separate instances in different PoPs — we rely on request routing affinity to maintain cache hits. We also have a background mechanism for cold-start mitigation and a shared cache for some workflows, but we'll need to map that to your routing layer.
04:50 Nia (ZenithMesh): From a compliance standpoint — audit logs, retention policies, and the ability to run forensics on a per-tenant basis are must-haves. Can your platform export detailed per-request traces?
05:02 Priya (Redwood): Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-request traces (with sampling), and audit logs. For Private we can push logs to your SIEM via forwarders. We'll include retention SLAs in the SOW.
05:18 Jorge (ZenithMesh): On the integrations timeline — we are hoping to pilot with 3 ISVs in Q1. Is that realistic?
05:27 Alex (Redwood): Q1 pilot seems doable. Typical timeline: 2–4 weeks for initial onboarding and network setup, 2–6 weeks for integration, plus a 2-week pilot. Depends on the depth (VPC peering vs hosted).
05:40 Omar (ZenithMesh): We might want to run a small benchmark for latency-sensitive customers. Any recommended tests?
05:46 Maya (Redwood): We usually run a 3-test suite: 1) cold-start p99 under small qps, 2) steady-state latency with batching profiles (1–16), and 3) throughput cost run to measure tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens. We'll draft a plan.
06:00 Jorge (ZenithMesh): One of our ISVs needs a guaranteed p99 < 120ms for short outputs — is that in scope on your H100 quantized variants?
06:11 Maya (Redwood): Possibly for very short outputs with right batching and KV affinity, but on H100 the p99 might be ~80–150ms depending on model architecture and tokenization. We'd want to run a focused benchmark with their prompt templates.
06:25 Lena (ZenithMesh): Can Redwood expose model variants in your catalog via API so we can present them in our UI with metadata (latency/cost per 1k tokens)?
06:33 Priya (Redwood): Yes — model catalog metadata is available via our API and can be synced to your marketplace. We'll share an example payload.
06:42 Jorge (ZenithMesh): What about fallbacks — if a dedicated pool is saturated do you have a graceful fallback to a hosted lower-tier model?
06:50 Maya (Redwood): We support smart routing policies — you can set priority by latency/cost/region and automatic fallback to compatible variants. For strict isolation customers, fallback is disabled by default but can be enabled per-tenant.
07:06 Omar (ZenithMesh): On the channel side, what's the approval process for a marketplace listing? Is it automated?
07:12 Alex (Redwood): For partner marketplace listings we have a vetting process: security and compliance review, an integration checklist, and a short UI/UX signoff. After that we provide a listing package and optional co-marketing.
07:24 Jorge (ZenithMesh): Are there any gotchas we've seen integrating with other channel partners — things we should watch for?
07:31 Maya (Redwood): Two things: 1) assumptions about network affinity — if you assume stateless routing you'll lose prefix cache benefits; 2) billing model mismatch — e.g., per-token billing vs per-seat marketplace billing requires reconciliation.
07:45 Lena (ZenithMesh): Regarding billing, can your telemetry emit per-tenant consumption files we can ingest for billing?
07:50 Priya (Redwood): Yes, we provide usage exports (per-tenant) and can push to S3 or an API.
07:58 Nia (ZenithMesh): For enterprise customers we may need contract terms around data residency — can Redwood pin data for generation results to EU-only storage?
08:07 Alex (Redwood): We have region pinning options in Private deployments and can commit to EU-only storage via an SOW for Dedicated/Private. For hosted standard we have region controls but some logs may cross boundaries unless controlled.
08:20 Jorge (ZenithMesh): Great. Quick note — one of our concerns is partner ops overhead. If we co-locate, how much instrumentation do you require on our side?
08:29 Maya (Redwood): We ask for basic metrics exposure (node-level metrics), routes for control-plane callbacks, and access to your ops Slack or incident channel during onboarding. We can run with minimal instrumentation but it increases our ability to troubleshoot.
08:45 Omar (ZenithMesh): A question on upgrades: how do you handle model rollouts? If we list a model and Redwood pushes a new version, does it automatically roll for our customers?
08:54 Priya (Redwood): Rollouts are configurable: canary by percentage, per-tenant pinning, or manual. We'll honor partner pinning rules.
09:04 Jorge (ZenithMesh): Okay let's talk pilots — what would a small pilot look like for 3 ISVs?
09:12 Alex (Redwood): Pilot framing: 1) scoping call for each ISV to capture prompts/SLAs; 2) network setup (peering or mTLS); 3) run benchmarks; 4) joint go/no-go. Expect 6–8 weeks from start to completion if we do VPC peering.
09:28 Lena (ZenithMesh): We prefer short pilots; if we can keep the network part simple (hosted + allowlist) we can compress to 4–6 weeks.
09:36 Maya (Redwood): That works for low-risk customers. For enterprise customers requiring C2/C3 isolation we stick to private flows which take longer.
09:46 Jorge (ZenithMesh): Any immediate blockers you foresee?
09:50 Maya (Redwood): Nothing technical we can't handle. We'll want to verify IP plan and whether your Transit Gateway allows dedicated routing for partner-managed subnets. Also confirm if customers require customer-managed KMS.
10:04 Alex (Redwood): We'll follow up with a short checklist to capture those details.
10:10 Nia (ZenithMesh): We'll also need an initial security questionnaire — can you fill ours?
10:15 Samir (Redwood): Yes — send it over, and we'll have our security team respond. Usually a 5–7 business day turnaround for the full answers.
10:25 Jorge (ZenithMesh): Okay last bit — co-marketing and case study cadence? We usually want a joint announcement after pilot.
10:33 Alex (Redwood): Happy to do co-marketing; we'll pair PMM and GTM to scope an announcement plan if pilot goes well.
10:40 Omar (ZenithMesh): Perfect. That covers most of it for today.
10:44 Alex (Redwood): Quick recap of next steps: Alex to send checklist and SOC2 + partner one-pager; Maya to draft benchmark plan; Lena to provide infra diagrams; schedule tech deep dive the week of Dec 7.
10:58 Jorge (ZenithMesh): Thanks everyone, we'll review and loop in the ISVs.
11:03 Meeting ends
